body.statement: For every compact \(K\) on which the derived rank-stressed construction is valid, there are \(C_K<\infty\) and \(n_K\) such that, for every \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\in K\) and \(n\geq n_K\), the single total estimator \(\widehat{\tau}^{*}_n(x_0)\) satisfies \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{band}}}\mathbb{E}_P\left|\widehat{\tau}^{*}_n(x_0)-\tau_P(x_0)\right|\leq C_K\inf_{(h,k)\in\mathcal T_n}\left[h^\gamma+\left(\frac{h}{k^{1/d}}\right)^{\alpha+\beta}+\left\{\frac{1}{nh^d}\left(1+\frac{k}{nh^d}\right)\right\}^{1/2}\right]=C_Kr_n^*.\] It switches only through the deterministic exhaustive partition \((G_n,P_n)\), has bounded fallbacks on every sample, and neither estimates the covariate density nor assumes its smoothness. On the explicitly restricted class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{band}}\), it attains the optimizer-defined KBRW mean-absolute-risk benchmark without the density-estimation or density-ratio condition used in KBRW Theorem 2. This is a rate-and-construction comparison on the fixed positive-band class, not an assertion that either theorem class contains the other.
body.justification: The headline result stitches complementary density-free mechanisms into one benchmark-rate estimator on the explicitly restricted fixed positive-band class without a logarithmic transition penalty.
body.gap: The KBRW upper theorem uses a covariate-law condition, stabilized HOIFs cover only the below-rank global branch, and close-pair variance estimators do not target CATE; no paper supplies this exhaustive local synthesis on the fixed positive-band class, and no class-inclusion comparison is claimed.
body.consumer: Pointwise treatment-effect analyses can attain the published benchmark under a primitive positive design-density band without choosing or estimating a density model.
